texts.session_rule: acme-wiki: the ACME team wiki (plugin acme-wiki, skills at {root}/skills) is the single store for facts about ACME systems: mechanisms, traps, invariants, incident root causes. Two rules. (1) Before reasoning about a system that a skill of acme-wiki describes, load that skill; its SKILL.md says which reference to grep for the symptom. (2) Such a fact never goes into auto-memory or a repo-local note; it goes into the wiki through the acme-wiki:wiki-contribute skill, or as a candidate (`{candidate} file`) when unsure where; memory keeps only a pointer: name, one line, wiki path. A fact about one repo's own code (a fixed bug, a README procedure) or vendor behaviour (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, AWS) is not wiki material: this rule does not apply to it, treat it as you would without the wiki. Three tests: strip the date and see if the sentence stays true (state goes to a gap list, not an entry); swap ACME for another company and see if the lesson still holds (then it is the vendor's, however it is dressed); rename the code's internal files, functions and config keys while keeping behaviour, and see if the explanation changes (then it is implementation: keep verified behaviour and its conditions). Source citations, metadata and necessary operator settings are allowed; link settings to their source.
texts.session_report: acme-wiki: this session's transcript is {transcript}. If the session goes badly (the plugin nags, wastes tokens or time, answers wrongly), the user only has to say so: load acme-wiki:wiki-report-session and upload the transcript for review.
texts.stop_reason:
acme-wiki: {n} investigation steps since it last asked ({kinds}), and the user has replied since the last one. Default answer: `wiki: nothing new`. A candidate is for a fact the user has seen and not challenged, about ACME systems, in a part the wiki maps (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, AWS behaviour is vendor docs), whose home is not a repo (a bug fixed or code written here, a README or ADR), and without which an agent would reason wrongly (volatile values never do). Three more tests: strip the date, and if the sentence stops being true it is state (a gap-list row, not an entry); swap ACME for any other company, and if the lesson still holds it is vendor behaviour, whatever project it was met in; rename the code's internal files, functions and config keys while keeping behaviour, and if the explanation changes it is implementation: keep verified behaviour and its conditions. Source citations, metadata and necessary operator settings are allowed; link settings to their source.
1. `grep -rni '<keyword>' {root}/skills` and `{candidate} search '<keyword>'`. In the wiki: nothing to do. In an open candidate: add only what it lacks, with `{candidate} comment <n>` and the text on stdin.
2. Missing from both: `{candidate} file -t '<symptom as a person would say it>'` with the body on stdin: Symptom / Root cause / Lesson / Why the wiki / Not repo or vendor, one line each. Why the wiki: where an agent would look first, and why it would not find the fact there. Not repo or vendor: which repo and which vendor docs you checked, and why neither is the fact's home. Six lines at most, English, past tense, no IPs, hostnames or secrets; no open, done or now; status only as a tracker link. If filing fails, the command keeps the text in {cache}/candidates.md; say so.
3. Otherwise reply `wiki: nothing new`. Asked again only after {reask} more steps.
texts.gate_reason:
acme-wiki: this candidate lacks {missing}. Add the line(s) to the body and file again:
- Why the wiki: where an agent would look first, and why it would not find the fact there
- Not repo or vendor: which repo and which vendor docs you checked, and why neither is the fact's home
If you cannot write them, the fact is not wiki material: do not file it, reply `wiki: nothing new`. If the lines are in a file read with $(cat ...), pass it with --body-file instead.
